latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: T cell (CD4>CD8) and B cell periductal infiltration of lacrimal and salivary glands with progressive epithelial destruction; substrate of focus score and the principal driver of sicca symptoms
Plasmacytoid dendritic cell driven IFN-alpha pathway activation amplifying B-cell survival, BAFF expression, and autoantigen exposure; correlates with anti-SSA titer and systemic activity
Excess BAFF in glands and serum drives polyclonal B-cell expansion, ectopic germinal centers, and autoantibody production; the proximal driver of hypergammaglobulinemia, RF, and lymphomagenesis
Class-switched IgG autoantibodies against Ro52, Ro60, and La antigens; markers of disease but also pathogenic for fetal AV block and contribute to immune complex injury
Diffuse polyclonal IgG elevation reflecting B-cell hyperactivity; chronic high IgG load contributes to hyperviscosity and hypergammaglobulinemic purpura

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Ectopic germinal centers in salivary glands
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Tertiary lymphoid structures with follicular dendritic networks and AID expression in minor and parotid glands; histologic substrate for clonal B-cell selection and MALT lymphoma transformation

Type II mixed cryoglobulins (monoclonal IgM-RF + polyclonal IgG) precipitate in cooler peripheral vessels causing leukocytoclastic vasculitis, palpable purpura, glomerulonephritis, peripheral neuropathy; key marker of severe systemic disease and lymphoma risk
Recurrent crops of nonpalpable purpura over lower extremities driven by polyclonal IgG hyperviscosity and small-vessel inflammation, distinct from cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
CD4 T-cell predominant interstitial infiltration of renal cortex causing tubular dysfunction; manifests as distal RTA, hypokalemia, nephrogenic DI, and progressive interstitial fibrosis

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Distal renal tubular acidosis (type 1) from H+-ATPase loss
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Autoimmune attack on collecting-duct alpha-intercalated cells with loss of H+-ATPase causes inability to acidify urine; produces non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, nephrocalcinosis, and hypokalemic paralysis
Cryoglobulin immune complex deposition in glomerular capillaries with mesangial proliferation, double-contour basement membranes; presents as proteinuria, hematuria, hypocomplementemia, AKI
Lymphocytic interstitial inflammation predominantly NSIP, with LIP, OP, and UIP-like patterns; lower-zone reticulation, ground glass, cysts (LIP); progressive restriction and DLco decline

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Follicular bronchiolitis and small airway disease
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Lymphocytic peribronchiolar infiltration causing chronic cough, mosaic attenuation, air trapping, and obstructive PFT pattern; common pulmonary manifestation overlapping with sicca-related airway dryness
T-cell mediated dorsal root ganglion neuronal loss causing non-length-dependent large-fiber sensory loss, sensory ataxia, pseudoathetosis; relatively specific to Sjogren among autoimmune diseases
Cryoglobulin or immune-complex mediated small-vessel inflammation of nerve vasa nervorum producing axonal mononeuritis multiplex with painful asymmetric sensorimotor deficits
Distal autonomic and small unmyelinated fiber loss producing burning pain, autonomic dysfunction (orthostasis, gastroparesis, impaired sweating); often with normal NCS

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Central nervous system involvement (myelopathy, demyelination, encephalopathy)
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Myelitis (especially with anti-aquaporin-4 NMOSD overlap in SSA-positive patients), demyelinating white matter disease, aseptic meningitis, cognitive dysfunction; lower frequency than peripheral involvement
SSA-associated annular polycyclic erythematous plaques with elevated borders, often photodistributed; corresponds histologically to interface dermatitis; particularly prevalent in Asian populations
Symmetric small-joint inflammatory arthropathy resembling RA but typically non-erosive; morning stiffness, polyarthralgia in MCPs/PIPs/wrists; Jaccoud-like deformity occasionally
Recurrent or persistent firm enlargement of major salivary glands from lymphoepithelial sialadenitis; persistent unilateral enlargement is the dominant warning sign for MALT lymphoma

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Aqueous tear deficiency and ocular surface damage
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Loss of lacrimal gland function with reduced aqueous tear secretion → keratoconjunctivitis sicca, filamentary keratitis, corneal ulceration risk; quantified by Schirmer and ocular staining score
Reduced unstimulated salivary flow → cervical/root caries, oral candidiasis, angular cheilitis, dysphagia, taste loss; quantified by sialometry and unstimulated whole salivary flow rate
Anti-mitochondrial antibody-positive non-suppurative destructive cholangitis overlapping with Sjogren in 5-10%; cholestatic LFT pattern with elevated ALP/GGT, pruritus, fatigue

Clonal selection of marginal-zone B cells from chronic germinal-center activity → mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma (commonly parotid), occasionally transforming to DLBCL; lifetime risk ~5-10%, ~15-20× general population
Profound fatigue (the most disabling symptom for many patients) with weak correlation to organ activity; partly cytokine-driven (IFN, IL-6), partly central; captured by ESSPRI fatigue domain
Secondary Raynaud occurs in ~15-30% of pSS; biphasic/triphasic digital color changes on cold or stress; typically without significant nailfold capillary abnormality unless overlap with scleroderma
Mild leukopenia and lymphopenia are common; immune thrombocytopenia and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia occur in a minority; severe pancytopenia raises lymphoma suspicion

Cumulative effect of corticosteroids, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate, methotrexate raising risk of bacterial, viral (HBV/HCV/VZV), and opportunistic infection; B-cell depletion produces hypogammaglobulinemia

Chronic glandular T-cell help and antigen presentation drive local B-cell expansion and recirculation
Activated autoreactive B cells differentiate into anti-Ro/La producing plasma cells
Polyclonal B-cell activation produces nonspecific IgG elevation
Sustained B-cell activation in glands organizes ectopic germinal centers with FDC networks
Persistent germinal-center activity provides clonal selection ground for marginal-zone MALT lymphoma
Sustained polyclonal IgG elevation precipitates lower-extremity hyperviscosity-related purpura
Monoclonal IgM-RF + polyclonal IgG forms type II mixed cryoglobulins precipitating in cold vessels
Cryoglobulin deposition in vasa nervorum drives ischemic axonal mononeuritis multiplex
Glomerular trapping of cryoglobulin-immune complexes produces MPGN pattern
Lacrimal acinar destruction reduces aqueous tear secretion and damages ocular surface
Salivary acinar destruction reduces unstimulated salivary flow with cariogenic and mucosal consequences
Periductal lymphoepithelial lesions enlarge gland parenchyma; persistence raises lymphoma concern
The same epithelial-targeted CD4 T-cell response damages renal tubular epithelium
Selective autoimmune loss of H+-ATPase in alpha-intercalated cells produces distal RTA
Lymphocyte-mediated alveolar/interstitial epithelial injury produces NSIP/LIP/OP patterns
Peribronchiolar lymphoid infiltration produces follicular bronchiolitis and small-airway disease
T-cell mediated dorsal root ganglion injury parallels exocrine epithelial attack
Lymphocytic and cytokine-mediated injury to distal small unmyelinated fibers
Autoantibody-mediated and inflammatory CNS injury including NMOSD overlap in SSA-positive patients

Severe cryoglobulinemic vasculitis with renal/CNS/cardiac involvement carries high short-term mortality

Cumulative immunosuppression raises infection and second-malignancy mortality

Urine pH remains >5.5 despite systemic acidemia (positive ammonium chloride loading test)
Chronic alkaline urine, hypocitraturia, and hypercalciuria precipitate nephrocalcinosis/nephrolithiasis
HRCT extent of ground-glass/reticulation/cysts reflects ILD activity
Restrictive impairment progressively limits exertional capacity
Diffusion impairment is the most sensitive PFT abnormality in pSS-ILD
Airway dryness and follicular bronchiolitis produce chronic dry cough

Symmetric small-joint synovitis without erosions

Cholestatic pruritus is a hallmark symptom
Persistent germinal-center B-cell selection drives transformation, dominantly to parotid MALT lymphoma
Nodal expansion accompanies clonal lymphoid disease, particularly cervical chains
Fatigue is the most disabling patient-reported symptom
ESSPRI captures dryness, fatigue, and pain on 0-10 scales
Cold-induced biphasic digital color changes
Mild lymphopenia is common; severe lymphopenia raises lymphoma concern
Immune thrombocytopenia occurs in a minority
ESSDAI captures multi-domain systemic activity; rising anti-Ro and serologic activity correlate
OMERACT salivary ultrasound score (heterogeneity, hypoechoic foci) correlates with focus score
B-cell depletion and corticosteroid load raise serious bacterial, viral, and opportunistic infection risk

axes.shape_free_text: Chronic foreign-body sensation, burning, photophobia; waxes and wanes with environment but trends upward over years
Persistent oral dryness with dysphagia for dry foods, taste alteration, oral burning, dependence on water at night

Unstimulated whole saliva collection over 5 minutes; ≤0.1 mL/min is a 2016 ACR/EULAR criterion (1 weight)
Van Bijsterveld or OSS score for cornea/conjunctiva staining; OSS ≥5 in either eye is a 2016 ACR/EULAR criterion (1 weight)
Lymphocytic focus score on labial salivary gland biopsy; ≥1 focus per 4 mm² is the highest-weighted ACR/EULAR criterion (3 weight)
OMERACT salivary gland ultrasound (parotid + submandibular) grades 0-3 for parenchymal heterogeneity, hypoechoic foci, hyperechoic bands
Bilateral or recurrent parotid enlargement; persistent unilateral firm swelling is a red flag for MALT lymphoma
Submandibular enlargement, less common but supportive when bilateral and recurrent
Anti-Ro52/Ro60 IgG titer; positivity is the highest-weighted serologic ACR/EULAR criterion (3 weight)
Anti-La IgG titer; almost always co-occurring with anti-Ro and removed as standalone criterion in 2016
ANA positive (often speckled pattern, titer ≥1:320) in 70-80% of pSS
RF positive in 50-60%; high-titer RF is independent risk factor for cryoglobulinemia and lymphoma
Polyclonal IgG; chronic elevation common (>16 g/L); falls with rituximab
Often modestly elevated as part of polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia
Monoclonal band on serum/urine immunofixation (often IgM-kappa) is a major lymphoma risk factor
Type II mixed cryoglobulin (monoclonal IgM-RF + polyclonal IgG); low C4 alongside
Quantitative cryocrit; persistence and high cryocrit predict vasculitic complications and lymphoma
Often normal or mildly low; modest decrease in cryoglobulinemic flare
Disproportionately low C4 is the most useful complement marker; persistent low C4 is a major lymphoma and adverse-outcome predictor
PBMC IFN-stimulated gene panel score; high IFN signature correlates with anti-Ro positivity and disease activity
EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index, 12 domains, range 0-123; ≥5 = moderate, ≥14 = high; clinical trial primary endpoint surrogate
Patient-reported index (dryness, fatigue, pain) on 0-10 each, mean 0-10
Often elevated (driven by hypergammaglobulinemia) with characteristically normal CRP
Typically normal or mildly elevated; high CRP suggests intercurrent infection or active vasculitis
Mild leukopenia common; severe cytopenia raises lymphoma suspicion
Mild lymphopenia in 30-50%; severe lymphopenia (<0.5) raises suspicion for lymphoma
Usually normal; ITP-pattern thrombocytopenia in a minority
Anemia of chronic disease typical; AIHA in a minority; severe drop suggests lymphoma or active vasculitis
Positive in warm AIHA cases (minority of pSS)
Stable in tubulointerstitial disease until late; can rise abruptly in cryoglobulinemic GN flare
Hypokalemia (often <3.0) in distal RTA; can present with hypokalemic periodic paralysis
Normal anion-gap metabolic acidosis (HCO3 typically 14-20) in distal RTA
Urine pH >5.5 in setting of systemic acidemia (or after ammonium chloride loading) confirms distal RTA
Medullary nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-phosphate stones from chronic distal RTA
Sub-nephrotic to nephrotic proteinuria in cryoglobulinemic MPGN; usually <1 g/day in tubulointerstitial pattern
Quantitative protein excretion; rises in cryoglobulinemic GN
Dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts in cryoglobulinemic GN; sterile pyuria possible in tubulointerstitial nephritis
HRCT extent of NSIP/LIP/OP/UIP-like changes; lower-zone reticulation, ground glass, cysts (LIP); progressive over years
NSIP > LIP > OP > UIP; LIP almost specific to pSS among CTD-ILDs
Most sensitive PFT abnormality in pSS-ILD; reduction tracks fibrotic progression
Restrictive impairment in fibrotic ILD; ≥10% relative decline over 12 months defines progressive ILD
Chronic dry cough from xerotrachea or follicular bronchiolitis
mMRC dyspnea progressively rises with ILD
Non-length-dependent loss of large-fiber sensation, sensory ataxia, pseudoathetosis, areflexia; hallmark Sjogren neuropathy
Asymmetric painful sensorimotor deficits in named nerve territories; usually with cryoglobulinemia
Distal burning, allodynia, orthostatic intolerance, anhidrosis from small-fiber/autonomic involvement
Pure trigeminal sensory neuropathy is relatively specific for pSS
Transverse or longitudinally extensive myelitis (NMOSD overlap), MS-like white matter lesions, aseptic meningitis
Anti-AQP4 IgG positive in NMOSD overlap with pSS; high prevalence in SSA-positive Asian women
Sjogren-specific annular polycyclic plaques with elevated borders, predominantly on face, photodistributed; particularly common in Asian patients
Palpable purpura (cryoglobulinemic) or nonpalpable purpura (hypergammaglobulinemic), predominantly lower extremities; flares with prolonged standing or cold
Cold-induced biphasic/triphasic digital color changes in 15-30%
Symmetric polyarthralgia/non-erosive synovitis of small joints (MCPs/PIPs/wrists), morning stiffness
Most common and most disabling symptom; weak correlation with ESSDAI
Cholestatic itch in PBC overlap, or skin xerosis from sicca
New/persistent cervical or axillary nodes raise lymphoma concern
Splenomegaly is uncommon at baseline; appearance may signal lymphoma transformation or AIHA
Cervical and root caries accumulating over years from hyposalivation
Erythematous/atrophic candidiasis with angular cheilitis is common in hyposalivation
AMA-M2 positivity defines PBC overlap (5-10% of pSS)
Cholestatic elevation in PBC overlap; ULN multiples track UDCA response
Mild ALT elevation in PBC/AIH overlap
Late marker in PBC overlap; rising bilirubin signals disease progression
Anti-centromere positivity in subset with prominent Raynaud, scleroderma overlap, increased lymphoma risk
Hashimoto thyroiditis coexists in 20-30% (TPO-Ab positive)
Celiac disease coexists in 4-15% of pSS (vs ~1% population)
Persistent unilateral firm parotid enlargement or focal mass on US/MRI/PET; warrants biopsy for MALT lymphoma
Histology of marginal-zone B-cell lymphoma with lymphoepithelial lesions; MYD88 wild-type, t(14;18) variable
Low-grade fever may accompany severe systemic activity, vasculitis, lymphoma; high fever should prompt infection workup
Significant weight loss should prompt evaluation for lymphoma
Anti-Ro positive pregnancy carries congenital heart block risk (~2%, ~10× if prior affected pregnancy)
Risk of fetal complete heart block in anti-Ro positive pregnancy, peaks in weeks 16-24

Annual transformation risk ~0.5-1%; lifetime ~5-10%; risk concentrated in patients with persistent parotid swelling, low C4, cryoglobulinemia, monoclonal gammopathy, focus score ≥3, ESSDAI ≥5, lymphopenia
Risk of severe cryoglobulinemic vasculitis flare (GN, mononeuritis, pulmonary)
Risk of progressive fibrosing ILD (≥10% FVC decline/12 months)
Progression to ESRD, mostly via cryoglobulinemic GN or chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis
Hospitalized infection rate, elevated with corticosteroids, B-cell depletion, hypogammaglobulinemia
Acute flaccid paralysis from severe distal RTA hypokalemia, especially in undiagnosed Asian women
Overall pSS mortality is similar to general population, but rises 2-3× with high ESSDAI, cryoglobulinemia, low C4, lymphoma, fibrotic ILD, severe vasculitis
Active untreated serious infection contraindicates B-cell depletion and immunosuppressant escalation

IGRA-positive status requires latent TB treatment before sustained corticosteroid/immunosuppression
Contraindicates teratogenic immunosuppressants (MMF, MTX, CYC, leflunomide); modifies HCQ continuation decisions
Modifies HCQ tolerability though clinically significant hemolysis is uncommon
Persistent monoclonality in salivary biopsy or peripheral blood is a strong lymphoma risk signal
Blood glucose, relevant to systemic glucocorticoid toxicity and diabetes context.
Absolute neutrophil count used for cytopenia and antimicrobial/myelosuppressive toxicity monitoring.
Bleeding hazard related to invasive procedures or extracorporeal therapies such as plasmapheresis.
Thrombotic event hazard relevant to IVIG, cryoglobulinemia, hyperviscosity, and vascular inflammation contexts.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Cryoglobulin classical-pathway consumption disproportionately depletes C4
Monoclonal IgM-RF is the structural component of type II cryoglobulin
Monoclonal gammopathy independently predicts MALT lymphoma transformation in pSS
Persistent low C4 is one of the strongest single predictors of lymphoma in pSS cohorts
Persistent or recurrent parotid enlargement is the strongest clinical lymphoma predictor
Cryoglobulinemia is among the strongest lymphoma predictors
Focus score ≥3 with germinal-center features is an independent lymphoma predictor
High-titer anti-Ro52 (>50 U/mL) is the principal CHB risk factor
Greater HRCT extent predicts lower DLco
Lower FVC predicts continued decline trajectory
Severe hypokalemia <2.5 directly raises paralysis risk
ESR-CRP dissociation is characteristic; CRP rises with active vasculitis or intercurrent infection but not chronic hypergammaglobulinemia

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: JOQUER trial showed no significant ESSPRI benefit at 24 weeks; modest real-world benefit on fatigue, arthralgia, sicca in many cohorts
Useful first-line for inflammatory arthralgia/non-erosive arthritis
Photosensitive cutaneous lesions respond well to antimalarials

failure_modes: retinal toxicity at high cumulative dose
treatments.context_specific_role: First-line for sicca-plus systemic constitutional/articular/cutaneous activity; weight-based dosing ≤5 mg/kg actual body weight to limit retinopathy

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Stimulates residual exocrine function; needs viable acinar reserve
Modest improvement in ocular dryness

failure_modes: no acinar reserve in late disease

side_effects.interpretation: Sweating, flushing, GI cramping limit dosing

treatments.context_specific_role: Symptomatic sicca; substitutable with cevimeline (M3-selective, fewer side effects)

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: M3-selective with longer half-life; better cardiac tolerance than pilocarpine

treatments.context_specific_role: Substitutable secretagogue, often preferred in Japan for tolerability

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Decreases ocular surface T-cell activation; reduces staining over weeks

treatments.context_specific_role: Moderate-to-severe keratoconjunctivitis sicca with ocular surface inflammation; substitutable with topical lifitegrast or topical 0.1% tacrolimus

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Rapid suppression of organ-threatening systemic activity
Bridge therapy in cryoglobulinemic vasculitis flare
Active untreated infection precludes high-dose immunosuppression
Latent TB needs treatment before sustained corticosteroid

treatments.context_specific_role: Pulse methylprednisolone 250-1000 mg/day x 3 then prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg taper for severe flare (cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, GN, severe ILD, myelitis); chronic use minimized

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Strong evidence in cryoglobulinemic vasculitis (mostly HCV-associated extrapolation; Sjogren-specific cohorts support same)
TRACTISS and TEARS trials showed mixed primary endpoint results but consistent benefit in subgroups with high systemic activity
Targets the clonal B-cell compartment driving lymphomagenesis
Mandatory antiviral prophylaxis (entecavir/tenofovir) before infusion
Defer until infection resolved
Particularly useful in NMOSD overlap

side_effects.interpretation: Especially with low IgG levels post-treatment

treatments.context_specific_role: Severe systemic Sjogren with cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, refractory MPGN, severe peripheral neuropathy, MALT lymphoma (with chemotherapy), NMOSD overlap; standard 1000 mg x2 two weeks apart

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: First-line non-pulse therapy for CTD-ILD; stabilizes FVC and DLco
Useful maintenance after induction in cryoglobulinemic GN
Teratogenic; switch to azathioprine

side_effects.interpretation: Bacterial and viral, especially with concomitant steroids

treatments.context_specific_role: ILD maintenance, cryoglobulinemic GN maintenance, severe systemic activity in steroid-dependent patients; substitutable with azathioprine in pregnancy

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroid-sparing maintenance for moderate systemic activity

treatments.context_specific_role: Pregnancy-compatible immunosuppressant maintenance; alternative to mycophenolate

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Effective in inflammatory arthritis component
Avoid in significant ILD due to hypersensitivity pneumonitis risk
Teratogenic; abortifacient

Severe CNS Sjogren; rapid suppression
Gonadotoxic and teratogenic; use mesna and consider fertility preservation

NMOSD/severe demyelinating attack rescue

May be used adjunctively, less infection risk than steroids

BAFF blockade reduces autoantibody-producing plasmablasts

treatments.context_specific_role: Investigational; promising in moderate-severe pSS with high systemic activity

Potassium citrate corrects both hypokalemia and acidosis simultaneously

treatments.context_specific_role: Distal RTA management; potassium citrate preferred for nephrocalcinosis prevention

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Used when PBC overlap is established
Improves cholestatic indices and survival in PBC

treatments.context_specific_role: PBC overlap with cholestatic pattern; 13-15 mg/kg/day

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Treatment indicated for symptomatic, advanced-stage, or transformed disease
Antiviral prophylaxis mandatory before B-cell depletion

treatments.context_specific_role: Watch-and-wait for indolent localized parotid MALT; rituximab monotherapy or R-bendamustine for symptomatic; R-CHOP for high-grade transformation; surgery/RT case-by-case

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Symptomatic relief; preservative-free preferred for frequent dosing

treatments.context_specific_role: Foundation of sicca management; preservative-free tears, gels at night, autologous serum drops in severe disease, scleral lenses for refractory keratopathy

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Conserves residual tears

treatments.context_specific_role: Refractory aqueous deficiency; temporary collagen plugs first, permanent silicone or cautery if effective

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hyposalivation removes natural caries protection

treatments.context_specific_role: High-fluoride toothpaste/varnish, frequent dental review, avoidance of sucrose snacking; substitutable with chlorhexidine, xylitol

female.trajectory_modulation: Strong female predominance; higher anti-Ro positivity

male.trajectory_modulation: Lower prevalence but possibly more severe systemic phenotype, higher lymphoma risk relative to female pSS

fourth_to_sixth_decade.trajectory_modulation: Peak onset 40-60 years; second smaller peak in adolescence

pediatric_onset.trajectory_modulation: Recurrent parotitis predominant, sicca often absent at diagnosis

haplotype_positive.trajectory_modulation: Strong association with anti-Ro/La positivity; particularly in European-descent populations

asian_susceptibility_haplotype_positive.trajectory_modulation: Predominant susceptibility allele in Japanese and Han Chinese populations

positive_family_history.trajectory_modulation: Higher concordance for SLE, autoimmune thyroid, RA in first-degree relatives

ebv_seropositive_high_titer.trajectory_modulation: EBV epigenetic/molecular mimicry implicated in glandular initiation

high_titer.trajectory_modulation: Predicts higher ESSDAI, more systemic involvement, ILD, CHB risk in pregnancy

low_C4.trajectory_modulation: Strong predictor of cryoglobulinemia, lymphoma transformation, mortality

current_smoker.trajectory_modulation: Paradoxical inverse association with pSS incidence in some cohorts; worsens ILD progression and accelerates dental damage

systemic_lupus_overlap.trajectory_modulation: Secondary Sjogren in 10-30% of SLE; consider SLE-driven flares as competing explanation

rheumatoid_arthritis_overlap.trajectory_modulation: Secondary Sjogren in 20-30% of RA; arthritis driver predominantly RA-pattern

systemic_sclerosis_overlap.trajectory_modulation: Anti-centromere positive Sjogren may be early scleroderma; nailfold capillaroscopy and skin exam

hashimoto_present.trajectory_modulation: Higher fatigue burden; ensure euthyroid before attributing fatigue to pSS alone

celiac_present.trajectory_modulation: Iron/folate deficiency may amplify fatigue and anemia

hcv_positive.trajectory_modulation: HCV-associated sicca/cryoglobulinemia mimics pSS; treat HCV first; reclassify if cryoglobulinemia is HCV-driven

hbv_positive.trajectory_modulation: Mandatory antiviral prophylaxis prior to rituximab; alters treatment plan

east_asian.trajectory_modulation: Higher prevalence of distal RTA, annular erythema, NMOSD overlap; anti-Ro52 high-titer phenotype prominent

currently_pregnant_anti_Ro_positive.trajectory_modulation: CHB risk window 16-24 weeks; serial fetal echo, hydroxychloroquine continuation reduces recurrence in prior-affected pregnancies

supportive_care: Preservative-free artificial tears, gel at bedtime, autologous serum tears for severe ocular surface disease, scleral contact lenses for refractory cases
Sugar-free gum and lozenges (xylitol-based) for stimulated salivation, frequent water sips, room humidification
High-fluoride toothpaste, professional fluoride varnish every 3-6 months, dental cleaning every 3 months, immediate restoration of cervical caries
Topical antifungals (nystatin, fluconazole) for oral candidiasis; treat angular cheilitis
Ophthalmology assessment with fluorescein/lissamine staining at baseline and annually; HCQ retinal screening at baseline and yearly after 5 years
Annual physical exam targeting cervical/axillary lymph nodes, parotid glands, spleen; persistent unilateral parotid enlargement triggers ultrasound and biopsy
Periodic monitoring of CBC, LFTs, creatinine, urinalysis with protein/creatinine ratio, complement C3/C4, IgG, ESR, CRP; frequency guided by ESSDAI
Baseline and annual high-resolution chest CT with pulmonary function testing including DLco for ILD surveillance in symptomatic patients
Pneumococcal (PCV13/PCV20 then PPSV23), annual influenza (inactivated), shingles (recombinant zoster), and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination; live vaccines avoided on significant immunosuppression
Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) when on prednisone ≥20 mg/day for ≥4 weeks plus second immunosuppressant or rituximab+cyclophosphamide combination
HBV serology and antiviral prophylaxis (entecavir/tenofovir) before rituximab if HBsAg or HBcAb positive; latent TB screening before sustained immunosuppression
Bone health: DEXA at baseline of long-term steroid use, calcium 1000-1200 mg + vitamin D 800-1000 IU, bisphosphonate when indicated
Cardiovascular risk reduction: blood pressure control, statin per ASCVD assessment given accelerated atherosclerosis with chronic inflammation
Fatigue management: graded exercise, sleep hygiene, screening for thyroid, anemia, depression, fibromyalgia overlap; cognitive-behavioral therapy
Genitourinary sicca: vaginal lubricants, topical estrogen for postmenopausal vaginal dryness, urology referral for urethral involvement
Anti-Ro positive pregnancy: hydroxychloroquine continuation, fetal echocardiography weekly from 16-26 weeks, perinatology comanagement; consider IVIG and fluorinated steroids if early CHB detected
Patient education on photoprotection (annular erythema, drug photosensitivity), keeping warm (Raynaud, cryoglobulinemia), and reporting persistent unilateral salivary gland swelling immediately
Multidisciplinary team: rheumatology, ophthalmology, dentistry/oral medicine, ENT, nephrology, pulmonology, neurology, hematology when lymphoma suspected, obstetrics for anti-Ro pregnancy
Psychosocial support: chronic disease counseling, peer support networks (Sjogren patient associations), screening for anxiety and depression at each visit
